free_tier.stated: ExaVault Cloud, the hosted product, was sunset. The on-premise appliance is still maintained and is free for up to 50 users with no expiry and no throttling. Capacity is the disk the user attaches to a machine they run; there is no hosted storage.

egress.terms: N/A — egress is your own VM's bandwidth. Note: 'Encryption at rest comes from your VM environment'.

interface_detail: sftp / ftp / webdav / rest (web manager, share links)
tooling: the user installs and runs the appliance image (VMware OVA, AWS Marketplace or GCP Marketplace image) on a rented or free machine; 4 CPU / 12 GB RAM / 100 GB primary disk plus a sized data drive; every installation needs outbound HTTPS to a license service and one source IP address
chaining: Unlimited free 'accounts' (appliance deployments) x whatever disk you attach. This is not free storage — it is free software for storage you already pay for. Worth recording because the category's free tier has structurally migrated here: the vendor monetises seats and support, not bytes.
limits_note: per-object-cap none imposed by the software; retention none; the binding constraints become your VM's disk and network. Paid tier adds SSO/2FA/syslog and >50 users ($99/mo per 50-user pack).

identity_cost.detail: unverified: how the free image and its license key are obtained was not seen; a valid license key file is required for free and paid installations

reliability_note: Free tier is 'never feature-degraded and never throttled' but ships no support channel and manual updates only.

How the free image and its license key are obtained was not seen, so confidence stays at reported.
